blocks.text: PERSONAL DEV FLEET · STRATEGY & MASTER PLAN
Personal Dev Fleet — Strategy & Master Plan

content.value: At its heart this is a simple thing:
your dev server is the place you work
— your data synced in from many datasets, Studio, Chat, your ledger — and other dev servers can
listen and take work from an orchestrator

through a protocol of four verbs. Everything else — the pricing, the waves, the machinery — elaborates that core without ever complicating it. This capstone carries the strategy; four companion papers carry the depth.
You don't buy a fleet. Your dev server grows one — one support at a time — and any AI can crew it.

content.value: Strip everything away and this is the whole system — small enough to hold in your head, which is the point:

blocks.caption: The entire protocol is four verbs — claim, pulse, stamp, close — over tasks routed by assignee.
blocks.source:
graph TD MAIN["YOUR MAIN DEV SERVER — the place you work
Studio · Chat · your data · the task ledger"] DS["many datasets
project A · project B · client X"] -->|scrubbed pull, per dataset, repeatable| MAIN ORCH["orchestrator"] -->|files an order = a task, assignee = a listener| MAIN MAIN -->|listen · claim · work · close| S2["dev server 2"] MAIN --> S3["dev server 3"] MAIN --> LT["your laptop"]

items.label: Simple
items.text: A dev server joins with one command; the orchestrator interacts with listeners ONLY by filing tasks and reading results. No bus, no custom API, no new concepts. Proven live with Claude and Codex.

items.label: Extendable
items.text: More hands = start another listener anywhere. Another AI = one adapter line. New kinds of work = an order is just a task — zero protocol changes.

items.label: Personal
items.text: The main syncs scrubbed data from MANY datasets (the shipped PDS pull; re-pull refreshes, merge-import converges) and is where the developer LIVES. The fleet is helpers attached to your home — invisible until you need hands.

content.value: Every future feature must survive one question:
does it add a fifth verb, a second bus, or a new concept the four-verb core does not need?
If yes, it is designed wrong. Elaboration is allowed; complication is not.

A developer should be able to multiply themselves without hiring, without babysitting infrastructure, and without fear that one agent's bad afternoon ruins the rest. The product is the third rung of a ladder that already exists — and it is
literally additive
: not a new SKU, but the $29 rung growing.

rows.value: One personal cloud twin; scrubbed pulls; reset fearlessly
Your dev server + N support servers that exist to serve it — capacity offload + concurrent agent work

content.value: The twin doctrine:
paid buys convenience, never capability — a free local fleet must always remain possible.
The isolation doctrine:

one worktree melting its box must never touch another agent — the unit of performance isolation is the MACHINE. The first keeps the ladder honest; the second is why supports are separate servers at all.
Everything shipped and everything planned is one of these five, made more perfect. Nothing else is load-bearing:

items.text: Orders are ordinary bp tasks routed by assignee. No message bus to run; cloud and local are the same wire; every action leaves an audit trail for free.
items.title: The ledger is the bus

items.text: Claiming a task acquires its blast-radius fence; overlap is refused 409 server-side; bp task frontier computes the maximal safe parallel set. Merge storms become structurally impossible.
items.title: A fence is a lease

items.text: A listener is alive exactly as long as its measured heartbeat is fresh. Stale = offline, fail-closed. The roster is the fleet made visible.
items.title: Presence is a heartbeat

items.text: Every order carries a weight class; every listener a size. The cheapest sufficient box wins — a big box is never wasted, a lean box never drowns. Proven 8/8.
items.title: The router is best-fit

items.text: Worktrees isolate code, not performance. CPU, RAM, swap and IO are box-wide commons — so heavy work moves to its own support server, and neighbour noise ends at the boundary.
items.title: The machine is the isolation boundary

content.value: The strategy was stress-tested through repeated correction — each fork below was decided, several were
reversed by evidence or by the owner
, and what remains is the set that survived:

rows.value: Hub-and-spoke: one main, N subordinate supports
Replaced the peer-fleet framing; supports exist to SERVE the main
Claim-CAS = the fleet mutex; workers need no Barkpark of their own
SUPERSEDED one-box-per-fleet: offload requires another box
Autonomy dial — full by default, tiered by choice
Full-auto makes gate hardening the safety case
Auto REFUSES until the multiplier is measured
People already queued; pilot lane before billing; never works-for-me quality
Claude + Codex proven; one adapter line per new agent
Visual setup in the Cloud console + CLI parity
The journey IS the acceptance test; extend console/bp/herd, never a bespoke console

content.value: The strategy's defining habit:
nothing was planned that had not first been made to work or made to fail
. One day carried the idea from paper to proven:

items.label: Protocol
items.text: Orders filed, claimed with fences, executed, stamped, closed — through the real ledger. The 409 refusal fired on demand; concurrent disjoint work ran side by side.

items.label: Endurance
items.text: A 4-challenge, 2-step dependent campaign with sealed answer keys: primes verified independently, a planted bug found and fixed adversarially, honest grades including a FAIL.

items.label: Efficiency
items.text: The capacity router proven: heavy→big box, light never wastes it, offline excluded, over-budget refused, spend-cap = zero ambition.

items.label: Neutrality
items.text: A non-Claude agent completed the full contract on the same ledger with only the exec adapter changed.

items.label: Discovery
items.text: The negative tests caught a genuine ledger defect (fences never freed on close — filed with repro) and a worker failure mode (backgrounded work produces nothing — now a hard rule).

content.value: A fleet that grades its own work must be incapable of dressing up a miss. The campaign's FAIL was reported as a FAIL, diagnosed, and became a protocol rule. That discipline —
every green must be one a broken build could not produce
— is inherited from the PDS epic and is non-negotiable in every wave ahead.

blocks.title: Why the misses matter as much as the passes

content.value: Pricing is honest and incremental because the architecture is: the base is the $29 dev server the customer already has; the upsell unit is
the support server
, priced by size class, elastic month to month because supports are disposable by doctrine.

items.label: Anchor
items.text: A fleet is N Personal Development Servers plus orchestration — legible to anyone who understands the $29 rung. The premium prices the conducting: fences, routing, the spend cap, the roster.

items.label: The variable that bites
items.text: Box cost is fixed and modest; token spend is dominant and volatile. Tokens are BYO-key or metered pass-through behind a HARD per-fleet cap that halts cycles — never bundled unbounded.

items.label: Go-to-market
items.text: Founder-first at flagship grade, with queued early users on manual provisioning + BYO keys BEFORE billing exists. Commerce is the last layer, not the first.

items.label: The showcase
items.text: The fleet is the feature that demonstrates what Barkpark is: the ledger, Chat, Studio, Cloud console and CLI all conducting real multi-agent work.

blocks.caption: The moat is the protocol and the ledger, not the model. Model progress anywhere makes the fleet better.

bp CLI + MCP spines · ledger · fences ·
presence · router · orchestrator"] CORE --> MAIN["your main dev server + supports"]

content.value: Strategically decisive: the fleet's value does not depend on any one AI vendor. The core — ledger, fences, presence, routing, grading — is Barkpark; agents are interchangeable crew. Every new frontier model, from anyone, makes the product
stronger
, not obsolete. Two spines carry any agent: the
bp
CLI for anything with a shell, and
bp mcp serve
for anything that speaks MCP.
Product stages and engineering waves, unified. The engineering waves (A–F) build the perfect machinery; the product stages (MVP-0/1/2) wrap it for people. They interleave on one timeline:

snapshot.title: DONE · PoC + skills + router + Codex proof + papers
MVP-0 · Visual setup + first offload + engine acceptance
C+D · Cloud add-support + durability (fence fix, spend cap)
E+F · Orchestrator at scale + THE SEAL

Kill a listener → OFFLINE exactly past its TTL
Measured capacity heartbeats feed the router live
Heavy→big, light→lean, driven by real heartbeats
The console journey; one heavy task provably leaves the main
A stranger walks it unaided; the main stays fast

close frees a fence; a killed worker's order re-opens; the cap halts a batch

Four-support concurrency with the cap firing
The two dials live; gate hardening for full-auto

first, and whenever direction is questioned

items.value: Every wave runs through bp-epic-cycle under the epic task — the fleet builds itself the way it will build everything else.
No wave ships without a proof that can fail; no green counts if a broken build could produce it.
Misses are reported as misses, diagnosed, and turned into rules — the FAIL that taught in-turn execution is the model.
Filed, claimed, fenced, stamped, closed — the same ledger the fleet runs on records how the fleet is built.
If a flow is not effortless for a stranger, it is not done.

content.value: A stranger with a $29 dev server clicks Add Support, hands the fleet a wish, and watches differently-sized machines — crewed by whatever AI they prefer — do real work safely, cheaply, and visibly, while their main stays fast.
Simple, safe, smooth, clever, everywhere.
That is the strategy, and every piece of it now has running code or a named wave.

PERSONAL DEV FLEET · STRATEGY & MASTER PLAN

Personal Dev Fleet — Strategy & Master Plan

Barkpark · the capstone paper · Rev 2 · 2026-07-22

At its heart this is a simple thing: your dev server is the place you work — your data synced in from many datasets, Studio, Chat, your ledger — and other dev servers can listen and take work from an orchestrator through a protocol of four verbs. Everything else — the pricing, the waves, the machinery — elaborates that core without ever complicating it. This capstone carries the strategy; four companion papers carry the depth.

You don't buy a fleet. Your dev server grows one — one support at a time — and any AI can crew it.

1 day
Idea → proven, running code
4
Verbs in the whole protocol
2
Agent kinds proven (Claude·Codex)
3
Rungs on the Personal ladder
6+3
Waves + product stages, unified

Papers in the constellation

  2. 2. The vision and the ladder
  3. 3. The strategy in five ideas

  5. 5. Evidence-led: proofs before plans
  6. 6. The business strategy
  7. 7. The provider-neutral moat
  8. 8. The master plan — one roadmap
  9. 9. The paper constellation
  10. 10. How we execute

The simple core

Strip everything away and this is the whole system — small enough to hold in your head, which is the point:

Simple4 verbs A dev server joins with one command; the orchestrator interacts with listeners ONLY by filing tasks and reading results. No bus, no custom API, no new concepts. Proven live with Claude and Codex.
Extendable3 axes More hands = start another listener anywhere. Another AI = one adapter line. New kinds of work = an order is just a task — zero protocol changes.
PersonalHome base The main syncs scrubbed data from MANY datasets (the shipped PDS pull; re-pull refreshes, merge-import converges) and is where the developer LIVES. The fleet is helpers attached to your home — invisible until you need hands.
The simplicity law
Every future feature must survive one question: does it add a fifth verb, a second bus, or a new concept the four-verb core does not need? If yes, it is designed wrong. Elaboration is allowed; complication is not.

The vision and the ladder

A developer should be able to multiply themselves without hiring, without babysitting infrastructure, and without fear that one agent's bad afternoon ruins the rest. The product is the third rung of a ladder that already exists — and it is literally additive: not a new SKU, but the $29 rung growing.

RungWhat you getPrice
Personal Localbin/barkpark up — offline, free foreverFree
Personal Development ServerOne personal cloud twin; scrubbed pulls; reset fearlessly$29 / mo
Personal Dev FleetYour dev server + N support servers that exist to serve it — capacity offload + concurrent agent workPer support server
Two doctrines govern everything
The twin doctrine: paid buys convenience, never capability — a free local fleet must always remain possible. The isolation doctrine: one worktree melting its box must never touch another agent — the unit of performance isolation is the MACHINE. The first keeps the ladder honest; the second is why supports are separate servers at all.

The strategy in five ideas

Everything shipped and everything planned is one of these five, made more perfect. Nothing else is load-bearing:

The ledger is the bus
Orders are ordinary bp tasks routed by assignee. No message bus to run; cloud and local are the same wire; every action leaves an audit trail for free.
A fence is a lease
Claiming a task acquires its blast-radius fence; overlap is refused 409 server-side; bp task frontier computes the maximal safe parallel set. Merge storms become structurally impossible.
Presence is a heartbeat
A listener is alive exactly as long as its measured heartbeat is fresh. Stale = offline, fail-closed. The roster is the fleet made visible.
The router is best-fit
Every order carries a weight class; every listener a size. The cheapest sufficient box wins — a big box is never wasted, a lean box never drowns. Proven 8/8.
The machine is the isolation boundary
Worktrees isolate code, not performance. CPU, RAM, swap and IO are box-wide commons — so heavy work moves to its own support server, and neighbour noise ends at the boundary.

The choices that survived

The strategy was stress-tested through repeated correction — each fork below was decided, several were reversed by evidence or by the owner, and what remains is the set that survived:

ForkRulingNote
Fleet shapeHub-and-spoke: one main, N subordinate supportsReplaced the peer-fleet framing; supports exist to SERVE the main
LedgerCentral on the mainClaim-CAS = the fleet mutex; workers need no Barkpark of their own
Infrastructure unitEvery member its own instanceSUPERSEDED one-box-per-fleet: offload requires another box
Who advances mainAutonomy dial — full by default, tiered by choiceFull-auto makes gate hardening the safety case
Who authors workWork-source dial — backlog · wish · autoAuto REFUSES until the multiplier is measured
First customerFounder-first at FLAGSHIP gradePeople already queued; pilot lane before billing; never works-for-me quality
Agent vendorProvider-neutral by constructionClaude + Codex proven; one adapter line per new agent
MVP surfaceVisual setup in the Cloud console + CLI parityThe journey IS the acceptance test; extend console/bp/herd, never a bespoke console

Evidence-led: proofs before plans

The strategy's defining habit: nothing was planned that had not first been made to work or made to fail. One day carried the idea from paper to proven:

ProtocolProven live Orders filed, claimed with fences, executed, stamped, closed — through the real ledger. The 409 refusal fired on demand; concurrent disjoint work ran side by side.
Endurance18 min unattended A 4-challenge, 2-step dependent campaign with sealed answer keys: primes verified independently, a planted bug found and fixed adversarially, honest grades including a FAIL.
Efficiency8/8 checks The capacity router proven: heavy→big box, light never wastes it, offline excluded, over-budget refused, spend-cap = zero ambition.
NeutralityCodex 1/1 A non-Claude agent completed the full contract on the same ledger with only the exec adapter changed.
Discovery2 real bugs The negative tests caught a genuine ledger defect (fences never freed on close — filed with repro) and a worker failure mode (backgrounded work produces nothing — now a hard rule).
Why the misses matter as much as the passes
A fleet that grades its own work must be incapable of dressing up a miss. The campaign's FAIL was reported as a FAIL, diagnosed, and became a protocol rule. That discipline — every green must be one a broken build could not produce — is inherited from the PDS epic and is non-negotiable in every wave ahead.

The business strategy

Pricing is honest and incremental because the architecture is: the base is the $29 dev server the customer already has; the upsell unit is the support server, priced by size class, elastic month to month because supports are disposable by doctrine.

AnchorThe ladder A fleet is N Personal Development Servers plus orchestration — legible to anyone who understands the $29 rung. The premium prices the conducting: fences, routing, the spend cap, the roster.
The variable that bitesTokens Box cost is fixed and modest; token spend is dominant and volatile. Tokens are BYO-key or metered pass-through behind a HARD per-fleet cap that halts cycles — never bundled unbounded.
Go-to-marketPilot lane Founder-first at flagship grade, with queued early users on manual provisioning + BYO keys BEFORE billing exists. Commerce is the last layer, not the first.
The showcaseBarkpark's power The fleet is the feature that demonstrates what Barkpark is: the ledger, Chat, Studio, Cloud console and CLI all conducting real multi-agent work.

The provider-neutral moat

Strategically decisive: the fleet's value does not depend on any one AI vendor. The core — ledger, fences, presence, routing, grading — is Barkpark; agents are interchangeable crew. Every new frontier model, from anyone, makes the product stronger, not obsolete. Two spines carry any agent: the bp CLI for anything with a shell, and bp mcp serve for anything that speaks MCP.

The master plan — one roadmap

Product stages and engineering waves, unified. The engineering waves (A–F) build the perfect machinery; the product stages (MVP-0/1/2) wrap it for people. They interleave on one timeline:

ProvenVisibleOffloadPilotsSealed

PERSONAL DEV FLEET · STRATEGY & MASTER PLAN

Personal Dev Fleet — Strategy & Master Plan

Barkpark · the capstone paper · Rev 2 · 2026-07-22

At its heart this is a simple thing: your dev server is the place you work — your data synced in from many datasets, Studio, Chat, your ledger — and other dev servers can listen and take work from an orchestrator through a protocol of four verbs. Everything else — the pricing, the waves, the machinery — elaborates that core without ever complicating it. This capstone carries the strategy; four companion papers carry the depth.

You don't buy a fleet. Your dev server grows one — one support at a time — and any AI can crew it.

1 day
Idea → proven, running code
4
Verbs in the whole protocol
2
Agent kinds proven (Claude·Codex)
3
Rungs on the Personal ladder
6+3
Waves + product stages, unified
5
Papers in the constellation
§
  1. 1. The simple core
  2. 2. The vision and the ladder
  3. 3. The strategy in five ideas
  4. 4. The choices that survived
  5. 5. Evidence-led: proofs before plans
  6. 6. The business strategy
  7. 7. The provider-neutral moat
  8. 8. The master plan — one roadmap
  9. 9. The paper constellation
  10. 10. How we execute
§

The simple core

Strip everything away and this is the whole system — small enough to hold in your head, which is the point:

Simple
4 verbs A dev server joins with one command; the orchestrator interacts with listeners ONLY by filing tasks and reading results. No bus, no custom API, no new concepts. Proven live with Claude and Codex.
Extendable
3 axes More hands = start another listener anywhere. Another AI = one adapter line. New kinds of work = an order is just a task — zero protocol changes.
Personal
Home base The main syncs scrubbed data from MANY datasets (the shipped PDS pull; re-pull refreshes, merge-import converges) and is where the developer LIVES. The fleet is helpers attached to your home — invisible until you need hands.
The simplicity law Every future feature must survive one question: does it add a fifth verb, a second bus, or a new concept the four-verb core does not need? If yes, it is designed wrong. Elaboration is allowed; complication is not.
§

The vision and the ladder

A developer should be able to multiply themselves without hiring, without babysitting infrastructure, and without fear that one agent's bad afternoon ruins the rest. The product is the third rung of a ladder that already exists — and it is literally additive: not a new SKU, but the $29 rung growing.

RungWhat you getPrice
Personal Localbin/barkpark up — offline, free foreverFree
Personal Development ServerOne personal cloud twin; scrubbed pulls; reset fearlessly$29 / mo
Personal Dev FleetYour dev server + N support servers that exist to serve it — capacity offload + concurrent agent workPer support server
Two doctrines govern everything The twin doctrine: paid buys convenience, never capability — a free local fleet must always remain possible. The isolation doctrine: one worktree melting its box must never touch another agent — the unit of performance isolation is the MACHINE. The first keeps the ladder honest; the second is why supports are separate servers at all.
§

The strategy in five ideas

Everything shipped and everything planned is one of these five, made more perfect. Nothing else is load-bearing:

The ledger is the bus
Orders are ordinary bp tasks routed by assignee. No message bus to run; cloud and local are the same wire; every action leaves an audit trail for free.
A fence is a lease
Claiming a task acquires its blast-radius fence; overlap is refused 409 server-side; bp task frontier computes the maximal safe parallel set. Merge storms become structurally impossible.
Presence is a heartbeat
A listener is alive exactly as long as its measured heartbeat is fresh. Stale = offline, fail-closed. The roster is the fleet made visible.
The router is best-fit
Every order carries a weight class; every listener a size. The cheapest sufficient box wins — a big box is never wasted, a lean box never drowns. Proven 8/8.
The machine is the isolation boundary
Worktrees isolate code, not performance. CPU, RAM, swap and IO are box-wide commons — so heavy work moves to its own support server, and neighbour noise ends at the boundary.
§

The choices that survived

The strategy was stress-tested through repeated correction — each fork below was decided, several were reversed by evidence or by the owner, and what remains is the set that survived:

ForkRulingNote
Fleet shapeHub-and-spoke: one main, N subordinate supportsReplaced the peer-fleet framing; supports exist to SERVE the main
LedgerCentral on the mainClaim-CAS = the fleet mutex; workers need no Barkpark of their own
Infrastructure unitEvery member its own instanceSUPERSEDED one-box-per-fleet: offload requires another box
Who advances mainAutonomy dial — full by default, tiered by choiceFull-auto makes gate hardening the safety case
Who authors workWork-source dial — backlog · wish · autoAuto REFUSES until the multiplier is measured
First customerFounder-first at FLAGSHIP gradePeople already queued; pilot lane before billing; never works-for-me quality
Agent vendorProvider-neutral by constructionClaude + Codex proven; one adapter line per new agent
MVP surfaceVisual setup in the Cloud console + CLI parityThe journey IS the acceptance test; extend console/bp/herd, never a bespoke console
§

Evidence-led: proofs before plans

The strategy's defining habit: nothing was planned that had not first been made to work or made to fail. One day carried the idea from paper to proven:

Protocol
Proven live Orders filed, claimed with fences, executed, stamped, closed — through the real ledger. The 409 refusal fired on demand; concurrent disjoint work ran side by side.
Endurance
18 min unattended A 4-challenge, 2-step dependent campaign with sealed answer keys: primes verified independently, a planted bug found and fixed adversarially, honest grades including a FAIL.
Efficiency
8/8 checks The capacity router proven: heavy→big box, light never wastes it, offline excluded, over-budget refused, spend-cap = zero ambition.
Neutrality
Codex 1/1 A non-Claude agent completed the full contract on the same ledger with only the exec adapter changed.
Discovery
2 real bugs The negative tests caught a genuine ledger defect (fences never freed on close — filed with repro) and a worker failure mode (backgrounded work produces nothing — now a hard rule).
Why the misses matter as much as the passes A fleet that grades its own work must be incapable of dressing up a miss. The campaign's FAIL was reported as a FAIL, diagnosed, and became a protocol rule. That discipline — every green must be one a broken build could not produce — is inherited from the PDS epic and is non-negotiable in every wave ahead.
§

The business strategy

Pricing is honest and incremental because the architecture is: the base is the $29 dev server the customer already has; the upsell unit is the support server, priced by size class, elastic month to month because supports are disposable by doctrine.

Anchor
The ladder A fleet is N Personal Development Servers plus orchestration — legible to anyone who understands the $29 rung. The premium prices the conducting: fences, routing, the spend cap, the roster.
The variable that bites
Tokens Box cost is fixed and modest; token spend is dominant and volatile. Tokens are BYO-key or metered pass-through behind a HARD per-fleet cap that halts cycles — never bundled unbounded.
Go-to-market
Pilot lane Founder-first at flagship grade, with queued early users on manual provisioning + BYO keys BEFORE billing exists. Commerce is the last layer, not the first.
The showcase
Barkpark's power The fleet is the feature that demonstrates what Barkpark is: the ledger, Chat, Studio, Cloud console and CLI all conducting real multi-agent work.
§

The provider-neutral moat

Strategically decisive: the fleet's value does not depend on any one AI vendor. The core — ledger, fences, presence, routing, grading — is Barkpark; agents are interchangeable crew. Every new frontier model, from anyone, makes the product stronger, not obsolete. Two spines carry any agent: the bp CLI for anything with a shell, and bp mcp serve for anything that speaks MCP.

§

The master plan — one roadmap

Product stages and engineering waves, unified. The engineering waves (A–F) build the perfect machinery; the product stages (MVP-0/1/2) wrap it for people. They interleave on one timeline:
